nodes.label: Failover Library (project overview)
nodes.rationale: Spring Boot library that transparently stores referential service responses and replays the last known-good value when the upstream fails; entry point is @Failover on a concrete class method because the CGLIB proxy requires the annotation on the implementation, not an interface.

nodes.label: Failover Handler Chain
nodes.rationale: AdvancedFailoverHandler (observable reporting, RecoveredPayloadHandler, exception policy) wraps ScatterGatherFailoverHandler (per-entity slicing) wraps DefaultFailoverHandler (store/recover + expiry). Layering keeps each concern independently replaceable and assembled at one point, FailoverAutoConfiguration.failoverHandler.

nodes.label: Store Assembly Chain
nodes.rationale: AsyncFailoverStore wraps MultiTenantFailoverStore wraps the base store (InMemory | Caffeine | JDBC | custom). Ordering is deliberate: tenant routing must sit inside the async decorator so each tenant's store receives identical wrapping.

nodes.label: FailoverStore.find defensive-copy contract
nodes.rationale: find() must return a defensive copy because callers mutate the returned payload (setting upToDate, asOf); without cloning the mutation would corrupt the stored entry.

nodes.label: ConditionalOnMissingBean extension points
nodes.rationale: Every core bean is @ConditionalOnMissingBean so a consumer can replace any default by declaring their own bean; named beans are referenced from @Failover attributes (keyGenerator, expiryPolicy, payloadSplitter, domain).

nodes.label: Module responsibility map
nodes.rationale: One module per concern (domain, core, aspect, per-backend stores, async, multitenant, lookup, resilience, scanner, observable, scheduler, autoconfigure, starter, dashboard) so a consumer only pays for what they add; the dashboard is deliberately self-contained and does not depend on failover-spring-boot-autoconfigure.

nodes.label: Testing conventions (unit vs IT, AssertJ, async=false)
nodes.rationale: Unit tests are pure Mockito/JUnit 5; integration tests live only in failover-spring-boot-autoconfigure against real H2 and set failover.store.async=false so writes are synchronous and assertions deterministic. AssertJ assertThat().isInstanceOf() is mandated over Assert.isInstanceOf().
